findings.text: the 42-row arm is called "a live write-ordering fault", but I measured all 42 carrying no updated_at, no claim_token and no run_id while every current writer of 'exhausted' stamps updated_at in the same statement as the stage, so no current route is implicated by the row markers and the state is legacy rather than live — with the doc's own follow_on asking for a live route to be found.

"refine_stop_reason has exactly one read path" counts only workers.py:6924 and omits the projection at graph_ops.py:18144, which projects the field into the refine-name claim query's returned items; the conclusion that nothing gates on the field still holds, but the single-read-path claim is a miscount as written.

the writer map pairs the clear at graph_ops.py:10721 with reconcile_reviewable_name_stage (:14275), but the statement at 10721 is inside _lock_claimed_name_bindings (def at graph_ops.py:10589) and the function named at 14275 never touches refine_stop_reason, so a reader tracing the clearer lands in the wrong function.

justifications.durability: nothing regresses the census if it rots — no test or code artifact carries the predicate, and audit-doc, the only standing structural gate, passes the two HTML artifacts while failing this markdown file and its siblings identically on missing meta, so it is not a value gate.
